A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V2Drop work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image/video benchmark evaluations, latency and memory measurements, and ablations in Tables 1–8 and associated figures.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen2-VL video results, DART comparisons, and quantitative positional-retention measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions use adjacent-layer variation, L2 distance by default, top-K selection, and progressive token dropping. Algorithm 1 and the appendix's LLaVA pruning configuration remain unchanged. Generalizing layer indices in the main text does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The same ten image/video benchmarks and task coverage are retained. Qwen2-VL video evaluation uses already-covered MVBench and VideoMME; the positional-bias analysis reuses TextVQA, POPE, and MME. These extend model settings and analyses without introducing new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds DART to the Qwen2-VL image comparisons in Table 2, where v1 compared only against FastV. DART also participates in the new Qwen2-VL video comparison in Table 3. Other existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B video evaluation at 20% average token retention. Figure 3 and Appendix D introduce a diagnostic protocol using 50% pruning at the third layer and ten token-position intervals across two models. Existing benchmark configurations are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 quantitatively tests positional retention bias across two models and three datasets, supplementing v1's illustrative heatmaps. V2 also adds computational-overhead accounting. The existing metric, layer-selection, and progressive-dropping ablations and visualization examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new retention probabilities describe token-position distributions, not uncertainty estimates; existing layer-variation displays are retained.

E6.justification: V2 adds DART image scores, positional-retention distributions, and Qwen2-VL video results: Table 3 reports 93.3% normalized average performance for V2Drop versus 90.5% for DART and 81.3% for FastV at 20% retention. Existing benchmark and efficiency scores remain. The layer-selection summary changes from 96.9% to 97.3% despite unchanged appendix values.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Section 3.4 and Appendix E with Jacobian-based definitions, smoothness and bounded-Jacobian assumptions, a variation-impact theorem, a corollary, and a proposition claiming approximate minimization of output perturbation. V1 contains no corresponding theoretical analysis or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain variation-based token importance, progressive attention-free pruning, and favorable image/video efficiency tradeoffs. The abstract retains the same 94.0%/98.6% performance and 31.5%/74.2% latency-reduction claims. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds explanations linking token variation to residual attention/FFN updates and discusses smoothness, Jacobian sensitivity, and near-zero-Jacobian tokens. V2 also interprets its FLOP estimates as negligible pruning overhead. Existing explanations of positional bias and progressive selection largely remain.

D1.justification: Hardware, software versions, disclosed pruning percentages, and code access remain unchanged. V2 adds FLOP accounting but removes v1 Section 4.1's explicit definition of equivalent token count as retention averaged across transformer layers, reducing clarity about comparison budgets.

R1.justification: V2 refreshes related work with references including IPCV, HoliTom, InternVL3, and a token-compression survey, while removing DynamicViT, Sparse-Tuning, and several future-application citations. The broad positioning remains unchanged. DART's underlying paper was already cited in v1; its evaluated-baseline role is new.

P1.justification: Matched introduction, related-work, experimental-discussion, and conclusion passages are extensively rewritten or condensed. The appendix is reorganized from separate A–I sections into grouped settings, results, algorithm, discussion, and theory sections. Citation style and author footnotes also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds the positional-retention figure and Qwen2-VL video table, expands Table 2, and restyles tables with shaded rows and colored percentages. Existing figures are largely reused, resized, and relocated; appendix examples gain numbering. The underlying visual designs mostly remain intact.

improvement.justification: The DART comparisons, Qwen2-VL video results, and positional-bias measurements strengthen empirical support. However, Section 3.4 and Appendix E turn an operator-norm upper bound into approximate equality and then a lower bound without sufficient assumptions: variation can lie in the Jacobian's nullspace. This undermines the new theoretical justification. Together with the omitted equivalent-token-count definition, these problems create material tradeoffs whose net effect on overall quality is not reliably assessable.
